vsm1.9:84.1: 10. Muditā—“gladness” as one of the divine abidings is always in the sense of gladness at others’ success. Sometimes rendered as “altruistic joy” and “sympathetic gladness.”
vsm1.9:92.2: 11. Kiṇāti—“it combats”: Skr. kºnāti—to injure or kill. PED gives this ref. under ordinary meaning “to buy,” which is wrong.
vsm1.9:96.1: 13. All texts read kassa (whose), which is confirmed in the quotation translated in note 20. It is tempting, in view of the context, to read kammassa (kamma’s), but there is no authority for it. The statement would then be an assertion instead of a question.
vsm1.9:98.1: 14. “Greed is the near enemy of loving-kindness since it is able to corrupt owing to its similarity, like an enemy masquerading as a friend” (Vism-mhṭ 309).
vsm1.9:101.1: 15. Paṭihaññati—“to be resentful”: not in PED; the verb has been needed to correspond to “resentment” (paṭigha), as the verb, “to be inflamed with greed” (rajjati) corresponds with “greed” (rāga).
